findings.title: Contradictory business rule on category list validity
findings.body: Business Rules section states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list' (line 148), but the Statuses / Enum Values section shows an initial list with five categories and then says 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list is not a complete AC6 record and cannot be marked current' (line 247). AC6 requires accounting for every candidate, including spec-AC-compliance and per-finding resolution, but the business rule implies list validity depends only on non-emptiness, while AC6 and the Statuses section make validity contingent on resolving open questions. These conflict on what makes a list 'current' or 'valid'.

findings.title: Missing URL-serialized state definition
findings.body: The spec introduces operator configuration for sweep enablement (AC18) but does not define the parameter key name used in URL-serialized state (e.g., query parameters, environment variables, or workflow inputs). AC18 states 'the concrete key name is a planning decision' but leaves it unspecified, forcing implementers to guess the serialization contract. Per the review checklist, URL-serialized state must have explicitly defined parameter keys and allowed values.

findings.title: Inconsistent treatment of 'ten' threshold
findings.body: The spec uses 'ten' as a hard threshold in AC15(b) and the Coverage Matrix (O11), but the Overview section (line 21) and Open Questions (line 719) describe it as 'roughly 10'. This creates ambiguity about whether the requirement is exactly ten or a flexible range. The business rules and acceptance criteria must use consistent, precise language for testability.

findings.title: AC6 incompleteness contradicts Document Quality Gate claim
findings.body: The Document Quality Gate states 'Internal consistency: Checked' and claims 'every objective in the issue body maps to acceptance criteria', but the spec explicitly acknowledges AC6 is incomplete due to unresolved Open Questions 1 and 8 (line 247). This contradicts the 'Checked' assertion and undermines the gate's reliability. The gate should either acknowledge the incompleteness or remove the 'Checked' claim.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'roughly 10' phrasing
findings.body: Open Question 4 (line 719) uses 'roughly 10' which is imprecise for a specification. Acceptance criteria require specific, testable thresholds. Replace with 'exactly ten' or define the acceptable range explicitly.

findings.title: Contradictory business rule about category list validity
findings.body: Business rule states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list' (line 172), but AC6 requires the list to account for every candidate including excluded ones, and the spec explicitly says the list cannot be marked current while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved (lines 327-328). This creates a contradiction: the initial list has only 5 categories but excludes candidates without recorded rationales, making it incomplete per AC6, yet the business rule implies an incomplete list is invalid. The document must resolve whether 'valid current list' requires completeness per AC6 or permits pending open questions.

findings.title: AC6 contradicts Statuses/Enum Values table completeness claim
findings.body: AC6 requires the recorded list to account for every candidate category considered, including spec-AC-compliance and per-finding resolution, with explicit exclusion rationales. However, the 'Statuses / Enum Values' table (lines 311-332) lists these two as 'Candidates awaiting a human decision' rather than as excluded with rationales, violating AC6's requirement that 'every candidate is either swept or explicitly excluded with a recorded rationale'. This makes the table non-compliant with its own acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Inconsistent threshold language for evidence tier transition
findings.body: The Evidence tier section (lines 565-572) states the transition to 'Real-PR evidence (measured)' requires 'at least ten pull requests', while AC15(b) (lines 691-694) states 'at least ten pull requests under the current recorded category list version have been sweep-enabled and reviewed, and their external-finding evidence has been adjudicated'. The spec must harmonize these definitions — the Evidence tier section omits the adjudication condition that AC15(b) requires, creating ambiguity about what constitutes fulfillment of the transition condition.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'roughly 10' phrasing in Open Question 4
findings.body: Open Question 4 (line 737) references 'roughly 10' dogfooded pull requests while AC15(b) and the Evidence tier section use 'at least ten'. This inconsistency undermines precision — 'roughly' suggests tolerance while the acceptance criteria require exact counting. Replace 'roughly 10' with 'ten' to align with the binding AC15(b) requirement.

findings.title: Open Questions section contradicts PR description's claim of resolved decisions
findings.body: The PR description states 'The issue owner answered every open question on 2026-09-26. The spec now states the decided behavior and its ## Open Questions section has been removed.' However, the spec file contains a full '## Open Questions' section (lines 749–820) with nine unresolved questions. This contradiction invalidates the Document Quality Gate's 'Internal consistency' check and makes the spec unimplementable as written.

findings.title: Contradiction between Business Rules and Open Questions on list currency
findings.body: Business Rule states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list is not a complete AC6 record and cannot be marked current' (line 464), but the '## Confirmed decisions' section in the PR description explicitly states decision #1 and #2 (which correspond to OQ1 and OQ8) were confirmed on 2026-09-26. The spec must either remove the Open Questions section entirely or update the Business Rules to reflect the confirmed decisions.

findings.title: Business Rule contradicts PR description's confirmation of decision #2
findings.body: The Business Rule states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved...' (line 464), but the PR description's 'Confirmed decisions' section explicitly confirms decision #2: 'Spec-AC-compliance findings — excluded' and decision #3: 'Per-finding resolution — excluded'. This creates an unresolvable conflict between the spec text and the PR's stated status, blocking implementation.

findings.title: Business Rule contradicts PR description's confirmation of decision #3
findings.body: The Business Rule states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved...' (line 464), but the PR description's 'Confirmed decisions' section explicitly confirms decision #3: 'Per-finding resolution — excluded'. The Business Rule's continued reference to unresolved Open Questions 1 and 8 contradicts the PR's claim that these decisions were confirmed, creating an implementation-blocking inconsistency.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for `unclear` outcomes
findings.body: The spec states in Statuses / Enum Values → Evidence tier that 'an `unclear` outcome is not terminal' and that 'a pull request whose compared findings carry an `unclear` outcome is not adjudicated'. However, in the Decision-gate consistency matrix under 'Evidence-tier transition', it states that a terminal adjudication requires every compared finding to carry a terminal outcome 'or the clean result `clean_agreement` is confirmed, so an `unclear` outcome is not terminal and its pull request does not count'. This creates ambiguity: the first statement implies `unclear` prevents counting, while the second implies it's an explicit non-terminal condition. The definitions must be reconciled to prevent inconsistent application of the ten-pull-request gate.

findings.title: Missing URL-serialized state specification for category list version
findings.body: The spec repeatedly references 'category list version' (e.g., AC3, AC7, AC19) as a key part of the sweep contract, including requirements for version identity, immutability, and usage in evidence recording. However, it fails to define how this version is serialized in URLs — specifically, what parameter key name is used (e.g., `list_version`, `sweep_version`) and what allowed value formats exist (e.g., semantic version string, timestamp, UUID). Without this, implementers cannot reliably construct or parse versioned links to the list artifact, violating the spec review checklist requirement for explicit URL-serialized state definition.

findings.title: Inconsistent use of 'real-PR' vs 'real-pull-request'
findings.body: The spec alternates between 'real-PR' (e.g., Use Case 6 title, Statuses / Enum Values → Evidence tier) and 'real-pull-request' (e.g., Overview, Business Rules, Acceptance Criteria). This violates the review checklist's 'naming and casing consistency' requirement and risks ambiguity. All instances should use the same canonical form — either 'real-pull-request' (hyphenated, full words) or 'real-PR' (abbreviation) — with one spelling used consistently throughout the document.

findings.title: Overly verbose phrasing in AC15(d) description
findings.body: The AC15(d) description contains redundant clauses (e.g., 'a defect reported by either configuration is matched to the same confirmed defect rather than counted twice') that repeat logic already established in earlier sections. This reduces readability without adding precision. Consider condensing to focus on the unique constraint being enforced (e.g., 'each confirmed defect counts once in the denominator, regardless of how many configurations reported it').

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for clean results
findings.body: The spec defines a 'clean result' as requiring confirmation by the 'recorded same-head external review' (line 1073), but the 'Evidence tier' enum table on line 1227 states that a clean result counts when 'every compared reviewer is clean, human adjudication recorded no defect for that head, and it is confirmed by the recorded same-head external review'. These conflict: the first requires the external review to exist and confirm cleanliness, while the second implies the external review is one of several 'compared reviewers' whose collective cleanliness suffices. This creates ambiguity about whether a pull request with no external review can ever be adjudicated as clean, directly impacting the ten-pull-request count in AC15(b). The definitions must align.

findings.title: Malformed category list definition contradicts itself on zero counts
findings.body: AC19 defines a category list as malformed if 'a finding-instance count is a positive integer — zero is not allowed' (line 1464), yet the 'Sweep categories (initial list)' table on line 858 shows `pr-head-push-order` with a count of `14`, `credential-pattern-gap` with `9`, `external-output-parsing` with `8`, `record-identity` with `7`, and `guard-fails-open` with `5`. All are positive integers, so this is consistent. However, the 'Excluded candidates' section on line 874 lists 'Planted-proof evidence (10 instances)' and 'Spec-AC-compliance (7 instances)' — both positive integers — yet they are excluded, not malformed. The rule must clarify that zero counts are malformed *only when present on the swept list*, not when cited in exclusion rationales, or the definition must be refined to avoid implying all cited counts must be positive integers in all contexts.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of 'unclear' outcome across sections
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' enum table (line 1522) states an 'unclear' outcome is 'not terminal', but the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' for 'Evidence-tier transition' (line 1625) says an adjudication is terminal only when every compared finding carries terminal outcomes 'or the clean result `clean_agreement` is confirmed, so an `unclear` outcome is not terminal'. This is consistent. However, the 'Business Rules' section on line 723 states 'an `unclear` outcome is not terminal, because the dependency contract defines it as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence', which matches. The issue is that the 'Use Case 6' description on line 452 uses slightly different phrasing: 'an `unclear` outcome is **not** terminal, because the dependency contract defines it as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence'. The bolding is inconsistent with other sections and may imply emphasis where none is intended. While not blocking, this stylistic inconsistency across core definitions risks misinterpretation by readers scanning for key terms.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for `unclear` outcomes
findings.body: The spec states in multiple places that an `unclear` outcome is not terminal (e.g., line 1073: 'an `unclear` outcome is not terminal, because the dependency contract defines it as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence'). However, in the 'Evidence tier' table's 'Valid transitions' section (lines 1197-1200), it says 'An adjudication whose every compared finding carries the `unclear` outcome is not terminal — the dependency contract defines `unclear` as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence — so that pull request does not count'. This is consistent. The contradiction arises in the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Claim admissibility' (lines 1359-1362), which states 'a head whose compared reviewers are all clean but whose human adjudication records a defect within the sweep's claim none of them reported being terminally adjudicated by a terminal miss record... rather than by a clean result'. This implies a 'clean result' (`clean_agreement`) is terminal, but the same matrix row also states 'an `unclear` outcome is not terminal', and the 'Evidence tier' table explicitly lists `clean_agreement` as a terminal outcome. The conflict is that the 'Claim admissibility' matrix row conflates 'terminal adjudication' (a state of the pull request) with the specific outcome code `clean_agreement`, while the 'Evidence tier' table correctly defines terminal outcomes as a set including `clean_agreement`. This creates ambiguity about whether a `clean_agreement` adjudication is terminal (it is, per the Evidence tier table) or whether the phrase 'terminally adjudicated' in the matrix row is meant to describe the *act* of reaching a terminal outcome, which `clean_agreement` satisfies. The matrix must be revised to use the precise, consistently defined term 'terminal outcome' and list `clean_agreement` explicitly as one of them, aligning with the 'Evidence tier' table.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of zero-denominator real-PR recall claims
findings.body: The spec states in the 'Business Rules' section (lines 1425-1427) that 'A zero denominator — no confirmed defect on those heads [...] makes recall not applicable: that measurement supports no recall claim, and it makes the variance result not applicable too'. However, in the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' for 'Claim admissibility' (lines 1391-1394), it states 'A comparative recall or variance claim whose confirmed-defect denominator is zero: that figure is reported as not applicable and supports no claim of that kind'. These are consistent. The blocking issue is in the 'Acceptance Criteria' section, AC15(d) (lines 1845-1847), which states 'a configuration whose denominator is zero (no confirmed defect on those heads) reports its recall as not applicable and supports no recall claim for that measurement'. This is also consistent. The contradiction is in the 'Coverage Matrix' under O5 (lines 2119-2121), which states 'a real-PR head set with no confirmed defect makes the variance result not applicable, supporting no claim'. This is correct. The problem is in the same Coverage Matrix row for O4 (lines 2115-2117), which states 'recall is read against the fixture's seeded defects, so a fixture comparison is never not applicable for want of a confirmed defect, while a real-PR head set with no confirmed defect makes the variance result not applicable'. This correctly distinguishes fixture vs. real-PR denominators. The blocking issue is that the 'Business Rules' section (line 1425) and AC15(d) (line 1845) define the zero-denominator rule for real-PR, but the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' (line 1391) and the 'Coverage Matrix' (line 2119) do not explicitly state that this zero-denominator rule applies *only* to the real-PR denominator and *not* to the fixture denominator. While the Coverage Matrix mentions it, the matrix is the normative summary for the gate and must unambiguously state the scope of the rule. The 'Claim admissibility' matrix row must be updated to explicitly say 'for the real-pull-request denominator only' to prevent implementers from incorrectly applying the zero-denominator rule to fixture comparisons.

findings.title: Overly complex and ambiguous definition of 'sweep-enabled review'
findings.body: The 'Business Rules' section (line 1138) defines a 'sweep-enabled review' as 'a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version as used'. This is clear. However, the 'Statuses / Enum Values' section's 'Evidence tier' table (lines 1180-1182) states 'Real-PR evidence (provisional) → Real-PR evidence (measured) when at least ten counted pull requests (sweep-enabled under the current category list version, with adjudicated compared-finding evidence) have accumulated'. The ambiguity lies in the interaction between this definition and the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' for 'Sweep enablement resolution' (lines 1305-1308), which states that an 'unrecognized' enablement value results in a non-sweep review. The spec does not explicitly clarify whether a pass that starts with an 'unrecognized' value but then degrades to a non-sweep review is still considered 'sweep-enabled' for counting purposes. The 'Business Rules' line 1138 says 'actually ran the sweep', implying it is not. But the 'Evidence tier' table's transition condition does not restate this nuance, potentially leading to confusion during implementation. The 'Evidence tier' table should be updated to mirror the precise language of the business rule, e.g., 'sweep-enabled under the current category list version and whose pass actually ran the sweep'.

findings.title: Inconsistent capitalization of 'Ronda-only outcome'
findings.body: The term 'Ronda-only outcome' is used with inconsistent capitalization throughout the document. In the 'Statuses / Enum Values' section (line 1533), it is written as '**Ronda-only outcome**' (bolded and capitalized). In the 'Business Rules' section (line 1455), it appears as 'a **Ronda-only outcome**' (same). However, in the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' (line 1362), it is written as 'a Ronda-only outcome' (not bolded, and 'Ronda' is capitalized but 'only' is not). For consistency with the rest of the document's terminology (e.g., 'Ronda finding rejected' is consistently capitalized), all instances should use the same formatting: '**Ronda-only outcome**'.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for `unclear` outcomes
findings.body: The Business Rules section states 'an `unclear` outcome is **not** terminal, because the dependency contract defines it as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence, so a pull request whose compared findings carry an `unclear` outcome is not adjudicated and does not count' (lines 1069-1073). However, the Evidence tier enum's 'Valid transitions' table (lines 1335-1338) states that an adjudication 'whose every compared finding carries the `unclear` outcome is not terminal — the dependency contract defines `unclear` as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence — so that pull request does not count, and a cohort of ten such pull requests does not reach this transition'. This is contradictory: the first quote says the pull request 'does not count', while the second says 'a cohort of ten such pull requests does not reach this transition', implying they *do* count toward the cohort but fail to trigger the transition. The spec must resolve this contradiction by consistently defining whether `unclear` outcomes prevent a pull request from being counted at all or merely prevent the tier transition.

findings.title: Missing URL-serialized state specification for category list version
findings.body: The spec introduces the concept of a 'category list version' (e.g., in AC3, AC7, AC19) and requires it to be reported in the review summary and used to decide evidence validity (e.g., AC15(d) 'read against the list version that head's pass recorded as used'). However, the spec fails to explicitly define the parameter key name and allowed values for this version when it appears in URL-serialized state (e.g., query parameters, path segments, or hash fragments). Per the review checklist, 'If the spec introduces URL-serialized state... the parameter keys and all allowed values are explicitly defined'. Without this, implementers would be forced to guess the serialization contract.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of 'sweep-did-not-run' record for malformed lists
findings.body: The Business Rules section states that when the list is 'unreadable, empty, or malformed', the pass 'records that the sweep did not run' (lines 1189-1191). However, AC19 (line 1510) states 'the pass reports no list version as used' in these cases. The Decision-gate consistency matrix (line 1425) then says the record states 'that the sweep did not run because its category list was unreadable, empty, or malformed (AC19)'. This creates ambiguity: does the record contain only the cause ('because...') or also the absence of a version? The spec should clarify whether the 'sweep-did-not-run' record includes the specific cause *and* explicitly states 'no list version' or if the absence of a version is implicit in the cause statement.

findings.title: Undefined 'confirmed defects' denominator for real-PR recall calculation
findings.body: AC15(d) states the recall denominator is 'the confirmed defects recorded for those heads' and defines membership via matching against the category list, but it never defines how to resolve cases where multiple adjudicators (e.g., external reviewer and Ronda) report findings that match different categories for the same underlying defect. The spec requires 'a defect reported by either configuration [to be] matched to the same confirmed defect rather than counted twice', yet provides no rule for adjudicating conflicting category attributions — making the denominator untestable and subject to arbitrary interpretation.

findings.title: Define the per-category pass record surface

findings.title: Remove Open Question 4 qualifiers from the ten-pull-request evidence-tier rule

findings.title: Make the matched sweep-off control requirement normative and add AC15(d)
findings.body: Confirmed decision 9 requires a matched sweep-off control for any comparative real-PR claim, and the PR description cites AC15(d), but the spec still treats the control as Open Question 9 and AC15 has no clause (d). Add an explicit acceptance criterion enforcing the matched-control requirement and remove the open-question wording from Use Case 6, Business Rules, and Evidence tier.

findings.title: Define accepted configuration values for sweep enablement
findings.body: AC18 says the sweep is off when the effective configuration value is absent, empty, or not a recognized on/off value, but it never defines which values are recognized. Implementers would have to guess the enum contract. Specify the allowed on/off values, their labels, and the behavior for each, or state the existing durability-switch value set if reused.

findings.title: Specify where a degraded sweep records that it did not run
findings.body: AC19 requires a pass with an unreadable, empty, or malformed category list to record that the sweep did not run, but neither AC19 nor Operational Visibility says which operator-facing surface carries that record. Define the surface, consistent with the per-category pass record decision, so the degraded path is testable.

findings.title: Require the own-repository label for real-PR evidence claims
findings.body: Confirmed decision 7 says every effect claim is labeled 'own-repository', but the spec only requires an independence caveat in AC16 and Business Rules. Add the explicit own-repository label requirement to the evidence-tier rules, Business Rules, and AC16.

findings.title: Define the counted pull request and dogfooded pull request terms
findings.body: The PR description and Brief Objective O11 use 'dogfooded pull requests', while the spec counts 'sweep-enabled' or 'reviewed' pull requests without defining either term. AC15's gate depends on this count and on adjudicated external-finding evidence. Define what pull request counts, what adjudication means, and use one term consistently.

findings.title: Align benchmark gate restoration with the deferred pass/fail contract
findings.body: AC17 and Use Case 5 say the seeded benchmark gate is restored once AC12 and AC13 seeds exist, but the PR description's deferred decision says the pass/fail contract of a restored gate is still deferred and no benchmark run passes or fails until thresholds are set. Reword AC17 and Use Case 5 to say the extended fixture may be declared ready as a gate basis, while the gate pass/fail contract remains a deferred decision.

findings.title: Clarify AC10 when uncategorized findings exist
findings.body: AC10 says a pass that finds nothing for every swept category publishes a clean result, but a pass could still publish uncategorized findings. Clarify whether 'clean result' means no findings at all or only no swept-category findings.

findings.title: Clarify the default-enablement gating conditions
findings.body: Business Rules says 'only two tests are gating' and then lists that recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence must be recorded and that precision must not have regressed. Reword the sentence to enumerate the exact gating conditions so readers do not have to infer whether evidence recording and precision non-regression are the two tests.

findings.title: Record Deferral Note D1 as confirmed rather than requesting confirmation
findings.body: The PR description says D1 was confirmed on 2026-09-26, but the spec's Deferral Note still says 'Human confirmation requested: yes — confirm that rebalancing stays out of scope'. Replace the placeholder-like wording with the confirmed decision and date.

findings.title: Add missing Matrix coherence preflight row to the Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs, including the evidence-tier transition table, the decision-gate consistency matrix, and operator-configuration precedence rules. The PR description's Document Quality Gate log does not include a 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row so the stateful-contract audit is visible.

findings.title: Define terminal miss record for a recorded sweep-off control
findings.body: The Terminal miss record section fixes only 'sweep_enabled_miss' and 'external_review_miss' and says both entries are recorded together. AC15(b) and AC15(d) make a recorded sweep-off control a compared reviewer and include its reported defects in the confirmed-defect denominator. If all compared reviewers, including a recorded control, report no findings and human adjudication records a within-claim defect, the control's miss has no terminal record. Add a control-miss code value or another explicit terminal-adjudication rule for this case.

findings.title: Define terminal adjudication for human-recorded out-of-claim defects when all reviewers are clean
findings.body: AC15(b) says a clean result requires human adjudication to record no defect, while the terminal miss record applies only to defects within the sweep's claim. If every compared reviewer is clean but human adjudication records a real defect outside the sweep's claim, the head is neither a clean result nor terminally adjudicated by the terminal miss record. This can leave an eligible pull request permanently uncounted. Specify an outcome or head-level record for out-of-claim human-recorded defects, or state that such defects do not block terminal adjudication.

findings.title: AC1 must assign surfaces for the unrecognized-enablement record
findings.body: AC18 and the decision-gate matrix say the unrecognized-enablement record is emitted 'on the surfaces AC1 assigns', but AC1 only assigns surfaces for the per-category pass record. Without an explicit AC1 assignment, implementers must guess whether the unrecognized-value record belongs in logs, check-run output, benchmark output, or some combination. Add the unrecognized-enablement record to AC1's surface rule or correct the cross-references.

findings.title: Reconcile AC1 surface rule for failures after a review is already public
findings.body: AC1's general rule says the check-run output carries the per-category record only where the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. Later, for failures after the review is already public, AC1 says the record is on the logs 'with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced'. If the write produced a success check run whose outcome is not a review, these statements conflict. Restate the post-publication failure case using the same outcome-is-a-review rule.

findings.title: Clarify AC8 baseline comparability and baseline-comparison configuration
findings.body: AC8 requires a repeated original-fixture comparison for 'baseline comparability' and Use Case 3 refers to 'the recorded baseline-comparison configuration AC8 defines'. AC8 also says the 2026-09-10 baseline cannot be reproduced and that no field is compared against its mutable alias. The result is an ambiguous, untestable requirement: it is unclear what 'baseline comparability' means, what configuration must be recorded, and how evidence is judged admissible. Define the required original-fixture comparison fields or remove the baseline-comparability language.

findings.title: Define whether failed sweep passes count as sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: The business rules define a 'sweep-enabled review' as a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category-list version as used. Use Case 6 and the evidence-tier transitions depend on the first recorded sweep-enabled real-PR review and on pull requests that carried such reviews. AC1 allows a pass that reaches review execution and then fails terminally to publish no review, and AC3 says such a pass owes no review summary or list version. The spec does not say whether such a failed pass can be a sweep-enabled review, where its list version is recorded, or whether it enters the eligible cohort. Define this case explicitly.

findings.title: Clarify compared-reviewer definition for reviewers with no findings
findings.body: One business rule says a pull request's compared reviewers are those 'whose findings its recorded evidence carries', but the clean-result rules require 'every compared reviewer reported no findings'. If a reviewer reports no findings, there may be no carried findings, making it unclear whether that reviewer is a compared reviewer. Clarify that a recorded no-finding result makes the reviewer a compared reviewer and specify how that no-finding result is recorded.

findings.title: Define effect of a no-finding sweep-off control on adjudication and tier
findings.body: AC15(c) says a sweep-off control recorded on a head inside a measured cohort can demote the tier because the control's findings become compared findings. It does not say what happens when the recorded control reports no findings. Since clean-result confirmation depends on every compared reviewer being clean, a no-finding control may still reopen adjudication or require reconfirmation. Define whether a no-finding control demotes the tier, how terminal adjudication is restored, and how it affects the count.

findings.title: Make AC15(d) category-membership rule testable and non-contradictory
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for a pass's own finding is determined 'by its per-category pass record entry', but then says no recorded entry decides membership and that an entry contradicting the objective test is a misrecording carrying no membership. It does not define how the objective match is checked, corrected, or recorded when the pass record and adjudication disagree. This cannot be tested as written. Make one artifact authoritative or define the objective membership test, the required adjudication field, and the correction path.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory attempted-run reporting rule in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says every attempted run under the variance configurations enters evidence, but also says an attempt run but not reported 'does not exist for this clause'. These statements cannot both be true. State that all attempted runs must be reported, and that an unreported attempt makes the variance evidence inadmissible or requires its inclusion.

findings.title: Require per-run defect-level results in AC8
findings.body: The business rules require benchmark recall evidence to report every individual run and the spread across identical runs. AC8 requires per-run recall, lowest/highest recall, standard deviation, and per-defect found/missed counts across runs, but it does not require the found/missed defects for each individual run. Aggregate per-defect counts across runs cannot reconstruct each run's result set. Add a requirement to record per-run found and missed seeded defect identifiers or equivalent per-run defect-level results.

findings.title: Define handling of degraded sweep runs in benchmark, precision, and cost evidence
findings.body: AC8, AC9, and AC11 require sweep-on and sweep-off comparison evidence. AC18 and AC19 degrade a pass to an ordinary non-sweep review when the enablement value is unrecognized or the category list is unreadable, empty, or malformed. The spec does not say whether a degraded run counts as a sweep-on run, must be excluded, invalidates the comparison, or is recorded as evidence degradation. Add an explicit rule for degraded runs in benchmark, precision, and cost evidence.

findings.title: Define content and surface of the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 permit a descriptive sweep-enabled real-pull-request miss record once the measured tier is reached without a matched control. No acceptance criterion or visibility section defines the required content, format, or record surface for that descriptive miss record. Define what it must contain, where it is recorded, and how it carries the own-repository label and independence caveat.

findings.title: Enumerate excluded never-found kinds individually in Statuses
findings.body: AC6 says the excluded entries are the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds, but the Statuses / Enum Values excluded-candidates section records them only as a grouped bullet. To satisfy candidate accounting, enumerate authorization bypass, data-loss overwrite, configuration debug default, and invalid range parsing as individual excluded candidates with their rationale.

findings.title: Replace approximate line references in the decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The decision-gate consistency matrix cites mirror surfaces with approximate line references such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. These are unstable and can drift. Replace them with stable section headings, business-rule names, or AC numbers.

findings.title: Enumerate recognized on/off enablement values or require the plan to record them
findings.body: AC18 says the sweep uses the same case-insensitive on/off vocabulary as existing operator switches but leaves exact values to the plan. For testability, either enumerate the recognized on/off values in the spec or require the plan to record them before implementation evidence is accepted.

findings.title: Align cohort cutoff wording between Use Case 6 and AC15
findings.body: Use Case 6 describes the eligible cohort as pull requests whose pass completed by a recorded cutoff before findings are visible. AC15(b) and the decision-gate matrix describe it as pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review under the version up to a cutoff before results are observed. The terms 'completed', 'carried', 'findings visible', and 'results observed' should be aligned to avoid cohort ambiguity.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful contracts, including Evidence tier transitions and a decision-gate consistency matrix, but the PR's Document Quality Gate log has no `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the required row after running the audit.

findings.title: Define how measured-tier cohorts accumulate after a cutoff
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the evidence-tier transitions require a closed eligible cohort with a cutoff fixed before any eligible pass's findings are visible and every member terminally adjudicated, but they do not say how to proceed when that cohort has fewer than ten counted pull requests or how later pull requests are added. A new cutoff after findings are visible would violate the rule, while keeping the original cohort open is not described. Define the cohort lifecycle or the ten-pull-request gate is not operable.

findings.title: Scope AC6 to the initial category list
findings.body: AC6 says the swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values and names the initial excluded candidates, but Use Case 2, AC7, and the revision-history requirements allow later list revisions that add, remove, or reorder categories. As written, a revised current list would fail AC6. Clarify that AC6 applies to the initial list version or define candidate accounting for revisions.

findings.title: Extend terminal miss record to recorded sweep-off controls
findings.body: AC15(b) and the real-PR business rule make a recorded sweep-off control a compared reviewer whose findings need terminal outcomes, but the Terminal miss record section only defines `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss` for a clean-head human-recorded defect. If a control also reported no findings, its miss is not terminally recorded, leaving the head's adjudication incomplete or contradicting the rule that both entries suffice. Add a control miss entry or state how the control is handled.

findings.title: Handle out-of-scope defects in clean and zero-denominator rules
findings.body: AC15(b) counts a clean head only when human adjudication recorded no defect, and AC15(d) says a zero denominator means no confirmed defect and external clean results are confirmed, but findings can be adjudicated `ronda_better` or `ronda_rejected`, or be uncategorized/out-of-scope, leaving no counted defect without a clean external review. Such cases are neither clean nor terminal misses, and the zero-denominator wording becomes ambiguous. State that clean and zero denominator mean no confirmed defect within the sweep's claim and define terminal handling for out-of-scope findings or defects.

findings.title: Clarify per-category surfaces for failures after public review
findings.body: AC1 assigns the per-category record to check-run output only when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review, but the later public-review terminal-failure case says the record is on the logs in either case while also mentioning whatever surface the check-run write produced. The decision-gate matrix example has the same ambiguity. State whether a landed review-outcome check run carries the record or the case is logs-only.

findings.title: Make sweep-claim membership decision testable
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership in the sweep's claim is an objective match against categories and failure shapes, and that a recorded per-category entry can be disregarded if it contradicts that test, but it does not define how the objective match is determined or how conflicts between record and test are evidenced. As written, two adjudicators may not derive the same membership. Define the evidence or procedure for the membership test, or make the recorded adjudication normative.

findings.title: Reconcile precision-pairing dimensions for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) says paired precision evidence need not match the real-PR comparison on reviewed target, fixture version, or sample count, but then says the fixture target and sweep arm are the only dimensions the pairing leaves out. AC9 and the claim-admissibility matrix repeat similar inconsistent wording. Enumerate the exact dimensions that must match and those that are exempt.

findings.title: Define tie-break for conflicting non-empty enablement sources
findings.body: AC18 resolves the effective value from the highest-precedence source but groups environment or workflow input over the operator config file without saying which wins if both supply different non-empty values. If existing Ronda precedence already defines it, cite that rule; otherwise specify the tie-break.

findings.title: Define how matched sweep-off controls are recorded without publication
findings.body: AC15(d) requires a matched sweep-off control on real pull-request heads that is recorded but not published, but the spec otherwise requires one published review per head for passes that reach publication and does not define a non-publishing review path for real PRs. Explain the product mechanism or evidence surface for such controls, or state that benchmark/offline runs satisfy this and how they are tied to real heads.

findings.title: Require control run set to be fixed before sweep-on results are visible
findings.body: AC15(d) fixes the matched control's run set only before any control result is observed, while its rationale says outcome-aware selection after sweep-on results are visible must be prevented. If the run count or window is chosen after sweep-on results are known, selection bias remains. Require the control run set to be recorded before sweep-on results are visible or justify the weaker rule.

findings.title: Define consequence of eligible pull requests lacking external review
findings.body: AC15(b) says a pull request with no external review recorded is not adjudicated, while every member of a closed cohort must be terminally adjudicated before the measured tier is assigned. If any eligible pull request lacks an external review, the cohort can be blocked indefinitely. State whether such pull requests can be excluded, how the cohort is repaired, or that this block is intentional.

findings.title: Clarify baseline comparability when the 2026-09-10 baseline is not reproducible
findings.body: AC8 and Use Case 3 require baseline comparability for the original-thirteen subset but also state that the 2026-09-10 baseline cannot be reproduced and no field is compared against its mutable alias. Clarify whether 'baseline comparability' means a new same-configuration original-fixture comparison rather than comparison to the 2026-09-10 figures.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful contracts, including evidence-tier transitions, adjudication terminality, and the decision-gate matrix, but the PR's Document Quality Gate log has no Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit or a reasoned Not applicable. Run the six-check audit and add the required row before approval.

findings.title: Define how real-PR controls and repeated runs are recorded without publishing
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off controls and repeated identical runs on the same real-PR heads for comparative recall, variance, and cost claims, and say controls are recorded but not published. AC2 and the business rules preserve the existing one-review-per-head publication contract and do not define a non-publishing real-PR pass or its record surfaces. Add an explicit contract for control and repeated-run execution, publication eligibility, surfaces, and interaction with supersede/skip, or remove those claim requirements.

findings.title: Handle terminal miss records when a sweep-off control is clean
findings.body: The terminal miss record defines only sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss, but a recorded sweep-off control can be a compared reviewer. If all compared reviewers reported no findings and human adjudication records a defect, the spec does not say how the control's miss is terminally recorded or counted in AC15(d). Define a control miss entry or state how the control is adjudicated and counted.

findings.title: Make sweep-claim membership test operational
findings.body: AC15(d) makes claim membership depend on an objective match and says a recorded entry contradicting that test is a misrecording carrying no membership, but it does not define how adjudicators determine, verify, or correct that objective match. Replace the circular language with a concrete rule identifying the recorded field that decides membership and the handling of missing or conflicting entries.

findings.title: Define required category field for adjudicated non-pass findings
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for external findings and human-recorded defects to name the swept category for claim membership, but no criterion requires that field or defines the outcome when it is absent. Specify the required adjudication field and the default treatment when no swept category is named.

findings.title: Scope AC10 to sweep passes that actually ran the sweep
findings.body: AC10 says a review pass that finds nothing for every swept category and has no uncategorized finding publishes a clean result. For an enabled pass that degrades to an ordinary non-sweep review under AC19, there may be no swept categories, making the clean-result requirement vacuous or contradictory. State whether AC10 applies only to passes that actually ran the sweep and what a degraded pass reports.

findings.title: Remove restated code values or fix exclusive-site claim
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says it is the only site that fixes `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected` and that no other site restates the values, but AC15(d) explicitly restates both code values. Either remove the code values from AC15(d) and reference the enum, or correct the exclusive-site claim.

findings.title: Align PR description with AC15 counted evidence
findings.body: Confirmed decision 3 says the ten-pull-request count requires adjudicated external-finding evidence, but AC15(b) counts clean external confirmations, Ronda-only findings, terminal miss records, and other compared-finding outcomes. Update the PR description to match the spec's compared-finding and adjudication rules.

findings.title: Define counting for pull requests with multiple reviewed heads
findings.body: AC15(b) counts pull requests, while AC15(d) metrics and cost are per head and one pull request can have multiple reviewed head SHAs. The spec does not say whether a pull request counts once, once per head, or how multiple heads affect the ten-pull-request gate and cohort adjudication. Define the counting unit and aggregation.

findings.title: Make eligible-cohort cutoff verifiable
findings.body: AC15(b) requires the eligible-cohort cutoff to be fixed in advance before any eligible pass's findings are visible, but it does not define what visible means or what recorded evidence proves the cutoff preceded visibility. Define the event or timestamp that establishes visibility and the required record.

findings.title: Enumerate or stably cite allowed enablement values
findings.body: AC18 defers the exact on/off enablement values to the plan and only references the durability-mode switch vocabulary. Because enablement resolution has distinct recorded outcomes, list the allowed values in the spec or cite a stable normative source so AC18 is testable without implementation inspection.

findings.title: Define terminal miss record granularity for multiple defects
findings.body: The terminal miss record section describes a head-level record for a defect but does not state how multiple distinct human-recorded defects on the same head are recorded or counted. Define whether one terminal miss record per defect is required and how each record is associated with its defect.

findings.title: Define handling of failed attempted runs in fixed run sets
findings.body: AC8 and AC15(d) require every attempted run to enter evidence and fix run sets in advance, but they do not define how crashed, incomplete, or failed attempts are treated for recall, variance, and cost metrics. State whether such attempts invalidate the evidence, count as observations, or are handled in some other way.

findings.title: Define the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record
findings.body: The spec repeatedly refers to a descriptive sweep-enabled real-pull-request miss record but does not define its required content, format, or publication surface. Define what the miss record must contain and where it is recorded so AC15(d) and Use Case 6 are testable.

findings.title: Distinguish baseline comparability from baseline reproduction
findings.body: AC8 requires a repeated original-fixture comparison for baseline comparability, then says no run against the 2026-09-10 baseline is baseline reproduction. Clarify that the required repeated original-fixture comparison is not a reproduction of the recorded baseline to avoid confusing the two terms.

findings.title: Correct pass record timing wording in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership decisions are recorded with the pass record before review, but the per-category pass record is written at review time. Replace the phrase with at review time to avoid an impossible ordering.

findings.title: Define clean-result handling for out-of-scope human-recorded defects
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) require human adjudication to have recorded no defect for a clean head, but only define a terminal miss record for defects within the sweep's claim. If all compared reviewers are clean and adjudication records only an out-of-scope defect, the pull request is neither clean nor terminally adjudicated. State whether out-of-scope defects block the count or provide a terminal record for that case.

findings.title: Extend terminal miss record to recorded sweep-off controls
findings.body: Business Rules and AC15(b) make a recorded sweep-off control a compared reviewer, and every compared reviewer must reach terminal adjudication before a pull request counts. The Terminal miss record section only defines sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss, leaving the control's miss unrecorded when all reviewers reported no findings and adjudication records a defect. Add a control miss outcome or generalize the terminal miss record to all compared reviewers.

findings.title: Define how repeated real-PR runs are recorded without violating one-review-per-head
findings.body: AC15(d) requires repeated identical runs on the same real pull request heads for variance claims, and Use Case 6 refers to recorded but not published controls, while AC2 and the Business Rules preserve one review per head SHA and publication when the existing flow reaches publication. The spec does not define an unpublished run mode or how repeated same-head runs are suppressed and recorded. Specify the mechanism or remove the repeated real-PR run requirement.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The PR description's Document Quality Gate log lacks a Matrix coherence preflight row, but the spec contains stateful contracts: Evidence tier transitions in Statuses / Enum Values and the Decision-gate consistency matrix. Add the six-check audit summary or a reasoned not-applicable row.

findings.title: Specify recognized enablement on/off values
findings.body: AC18 and the Sweep enablement resolution gate depend on recognized on/off values but defer exact values to the plan, citing only the durability-mode convention. This leaves the enablement gate's allowed values unspecified for testing. State the accepted values or define them normatively by reference.

findings.title: Define benchmark cost aggregation for multi-head runs
findings.body: AC11 requires per-run differences in model calls per pass and elapsed time per pass, while Use Case 3 and AC15(d) describe a run's recall over a whole head set. If a benchmark run includes multiple heads or passes, AC11 does not say how per-pass cost is aggregated or paired. Define the aggregation rule or state that the benchmark target is a single pass.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory precision-pairing wording in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says real-PR recall claims pair precision evidence on category-list version and effective review configuration and not on reviewed target, fixture version, or sample count, but then says the fixture target and sweep arm are the only dimensions the pairing leaves out. These statements conflict about which precision dimensions may differ. Reword to list exactly the allowed differences.

findings.title: Clarify per-category surface when failure occurs after review is public
findings.body: AC1's general rule assigns the per-category record to check-run output when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review, but the public-review failure case says the record is on the logs in either case and only vaguely references whatever surface the write produced. State whether an existing success check run also carries the record.

findings.title: Define eligible cohort cutoff and visibility rule
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) require a recorded cutoff fixed in advance before findings are visible, but do not define the cutoff event or timestamp, what visible means, or how pass completion versus review publication determines eligibility. This makes the ten-pull-request gate hard to test. Define the cutoff field and inclusion rule.

findings.title: Make sweep-claim membership decision testable
findings.body: AC15(d) calls membership an objective match but says per-category records do not decide membership and a misrecording carries no membership, without defining how adjudicators determine the objective match or resolve conflicts. Provide a concrete matching rule against categories and failure shapes, and state how conflicting or missing records are handled.

findings.title: State outcome when adjudication does not name a swept category
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for external or human-only defects to name the swept category for claim membership, but does not say what happens when an adjudication omits a category or names none. Specify that such defects are outside the claim or must be corrected before the claim is read.

findings.title: Require control run set to be fixed before sweep-on results are observed
findings.body: AC15(d) fixes the matched control run set before any control result is observed, but not before sweep-on results are observed, while cohort closure is meant to prevent outcome-aware selection. Adding or sizing a control after seeing sweep-on results can still bias comparative claims. Require the control plan to be fixed before sweep-on results are observed or justify the exception.

findings.title: Classify failures that occur while reading changed files
findings.body: AC1 covers failures before changed files are read and failures after a review request, but does not classify failures during changed-file reading or after review execution starts but before a request is issued. State whether these passes emit no record, an empty record, or not determined.

findings.title: Define terminal miss record handling for multiple human-recorded defects
findings.body: Use Case 6, AC15(b), and the Terminal miss record section describe a single recorded defect on a clean head. If human adjudication records multiple defects none of which were reported, the spec does not say whether one record with multiple entries or multiple records are required. Define the structure.

findings.title: Clarify whether terminally failed passes count as sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: Business Rules define a sweep-enabled review as a review whose pass ran the sweep and reported a list version, while AC1 and Operational Visibility can log sweep metadata for passes that fail terminally and publish no review. State that only published reviews count toward tiers and the ten-pull-request gate, or clarify the intended treatment.

findings.title: Limit AC10 clean-result rule to sweep passes
findings.body: AC10 says a review pass that finds nothing for every swept category publishes a clean result, but does not explicitly say it applies only when the sweep ran. With a disabled or degraded pass, the swept-category set may be empty. Clarify that AC10 governs sweep passes that reach review execution.

findings.title: Use a single confirmed-defect denominator in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) refers to a configuration whose denominator is zero, but the confirmed-defect denominator is defined by heads and is common to configurations. Reword to avoid implying configuration-specific denominators.

findings.title: Remove duplicated 'used. used.' in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains the fragment 'used. used.' after the sentence about recording the category-list version and effective review configuration. Remove the duplication.

findings.title: Remove stray sentence in Claim admissibility matrix row
findings.body: The Claim admissibility row ends with 'they do not pair the claim.' after the control-rerun example. The fragment appears leftover and is not tied to a rule. Remove or integrate it.

findings.title: Clarify 'only two tests' default-enablement gate
findings.body: The default-enablement business rule says only two tests are gating but then lists recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence plus precision regression. Reword to name the two gate conditions unambiguously.

findings.title: Move low-level failure mechanics out of product spec
findings.body: AC1 and Operational Visibility prescribe process exit codes, bounded retries, and check-run recovery state. If these are not product requirements, state them as existing behavior or move them to design/plan.

findings.title: Clarify 'number of runs per configuration' for matched control
findings.body: AC15(d) says the matched control's run set records its number of runs per configuration, but the matched control is the sweep-off configuration. Clarify whether this refers to the control alone or to both configurations in a repeated-run comparison.

findings.title: Correct 'pass record before review' wording
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership decisions are recorded 'the pass record before review', but AC1 and AC20 say the per-category pass record is written at review time. Correct the phrase to before adjudication or at review time.

findings.title: Identify the documentation required by AC17
findings.body: AC17 requires that documentation state the benchmark is not a regression gate and that the gate contract is deferred, but does not identify which document must carry the statement. Name the target documentation or state that this spec satisfies it.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs (Statuses / Enum Values → Evidence tier transitions and Decision-gate consistency matrix), but the PR Document Quality Gate log has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row; the existing decision-gate matrix bullet is not the required preflight.

findings.title: Define adjudication for human-recorded defects outside the sweep's claim when no reviewer reported them
findings.body: AC15(b) and Terminal miss record only handle human-recorded defects 'within the sweep's claim'; clean result requires 'human adjudication recorded no defect'. If adjudication records a real out-of-scope defect and no compared reviewer reported one, the head is neither clean nor terminally missed, so the ten-pull-request count is undefined. State whether such a head counts as clean for measurement or define a terminal out-of-scope head record.

findings.title: Zero-denominator rule assumes clean external reviews and misses excluded-finding cohorts
findings.body: AC15(d) defines zero denominator as no confirmed defect and then says this means the external reviews' clean results are confirmed. That does not cover cohorts whose only findings are excluded outcomes such as ronda_better or ronda_rejected: the confirmed-defect denominator is zero but the external review was not clean. Define zero denominator solely as no confirmed within-claim defect or state how that case reports.

findings.title: Terminal miss record does not cover a recorded sweep-off control that also missed the defect
findings.body: Business Rules and AC15(b) make a recorded sweep-off control a compared reviewer, but Terminal miss record only defines sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss and says both entries are required. If all compared reviewers reported no findings, a control is recorded, and human adjudication records a within-claim defect, the control's miss has no terminal record. Add a control-miss code or state how the head is adjudicated.

findings.title: Clarify and make testable the confirmed-defect membership rule in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for a pass's own finding is by its per-category pass record entry, but also says no recorded entry decides membership and a misrecording carries no membership. It also requires two adjudicators to derive the same membership from category/failure-shape matching without objective criteria. State the normative membership test, how disputes are resolved, and where corrected memberships are recorded.

findings.title: Close the definition of effective review configuration
findings.body: AC9 defines effective review configuration as 'every setting that can change what a review reports' and then names prompt, inference parameters, and model identity. The open-ended phrase makes the pairing requirement untestable. Enumerate all normative settings or state that the named settings are exhaustive for this spec.

findings.title: Define how degraded sweep-on benchmark runs affect AC8 evidence
findings.body: AC19 degrades an enabled pass with an unreadable, empty, or malformed list to an ordinary non-sweep review. AC8 requires sweep-off and sweep-on benchmark runs with equal sample counts, but does not say whether a degraded sweep-on run counts as sweep-on, counts as sweep-off, or must be discarded and rerun. Specify the evidence treatment.

findings.title: Clarify whether unpublished superseded passes count as sweep-enabled real-PR reviews
findings.body: Business Rules define a sweep-enabled review as a pass that ran the sweep and reported a list version, while AC15(b) and Evidence tier count pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review. AC1 says superseded passes publish no review but still write logs. State whether unpublished superseded passes promote the tier and count toward ten, or only published reviews count.

findings.title: Define 'check run whose outcome is a review'
findings.body: AC1 and the Pass-outcome surface assignment gate make surface assignment depend on whether the pass's check-run write produced 'a check run whose outcome is a review'. The phrase is not defined and is not a standard GitHub check-run field. Define the condition or reference the existing contract term.

findings.title: AC18 opening sentence overstates per-repository control
findings.body: AC18 begins by saying an operator can enable and disable the sweep for the repositories a deployment serves, but later makes webhook enablement deployment-wide and puts repository-keyed webhook enablement out of scope. Reword the opening sentence to avoid implying per-repository webhook control.

findings.title: Define or replace 'dogfooded pull requests'
findings.body: Brief Objective List O11 uses 'dogfooded pull requests', but the spec does not define that term and otherwise uses own-repository real pull requests. Define the term or replace it with the defined term.

findings.title: Avoid restating code values outside the fixed enum site
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values → Adjudication outcomes says it is the only site that fixes ronda_only and ronda_rejected, but AC15(d) later restates those code values. Remove the code values from AC15(d) or relax the only-site statement.

findings.title: Use consistent term for completed review execution
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix uses 'Reached completion', while AC1 and Business Rules use 'completes review execution' and 'reaches review execution'. Align the wording to avoid introducing an undefined state.

findings.title: Handle equal standard deviations in variance claims
findings.body: AC15(d) says a variance claim is compared as a direction (higher or lower). It does not state what happens when the two population standard deviations are equal. Add an equal/no-direction outcome.

findings.title: Fix 'pass record before review' wording
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership decisions are recorded 'the pass record before review', but the per-category pass record is written at review time, not before review. Reword to avoid the impossible sequence.

findings.title: Remove duplicated word in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains the duplicate fragment 'used. used.' after the sentence about recording the category-list version and effective review configuration. Remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Remove stray sentence in Claim admissibility matrix example
findings.body: The Claim admissibility matrix example ends with a stray sentence 'they do not pair the claim.' after the control-rerun example. Remove it or attach it to the intended sentence.

findings.title: Replace approximate line references in mirror surfaces
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix mirror surfaces cite approximate line numbers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. Replace them with stable section or rule identifiers.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs, including Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix, but the PR's Document Quality Gate log has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the required row to the PR description.

findings.title: Align PR coverage matrix summary with the spec
findings.body: The PR description's Coverage Matrix summary maps O5 only to AC8 and O7 only to AC11, while the spec's Coverage Matrix maps O5 to AC8 and AC15(d), and O7 to AC11 and AC15(d). Update the PR summary or correct the spec so the visible objective matrix matches.

findings.title: Define terminal handling for human-only claimed defects when other findings exist
findings.body: AC15(d) includes human-adjudication-recorded defects in the confirmed-defect denominator, but terminal adjudication and the Terminal miss record only cover heads whose compared reviewers all reported no findings. If a head has other compared findings and a human-only claimed defect, no terminal record or outcome is defined. Add a terminal record or outcome for this mixed case.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off controls in terminal miss handling
findings.body: The Terminal miss record defines only `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss`. If a recorded sweep-off control also reported no findings and human adjudication records a claimed defect, the control's miss is not terminally recorded. Add a control miss entry or an equivalent rule so the head can be terminally adjudicated.

findings.title: Define clean-result handling for human-only out-of-scope defects
findings.body: AC15(b) requires human adjudication to record no defect for a clean result, while terminal miss handling only applies to defects within the sweep's claim. If all reviewers are clean but human adjudication records an out-of-scope defect, the spec does not say whether the pull request is clean, blocked, or terminally adjudicated. Define the outcome.

findings.title: Resolve AC1 check-run surface contradiction for public-review failures
findings.body: AC1 says the check-run output carries the per-category record only when the pass's check-run outcome is a review, but later says a public-review failure leaves the record on the logs 'with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced'. Clarify whether a non-review success check run may carry the record or whether logs are the only surface.

findings.title: Define an objective category-membership test
findings.body: AC15(d) requires category membership to be an objective match that two adjudicators can reproduce, but it only says a defect matches a category's description or failure shape. Define the test or evidence fields adjudicators use, or remove the deterministic reproducibility guarantee.

findings.title: Make category membership authoritative and correctable
findings.body: AC15(d) says per-category pass records do not decide membership and that a misrecording carries no membership, while AC20 requires published findings to appear in the per-category record. Define how incorrect category entries are corrected and which record is authoritative for measurement.

findings.title: Define membership reconciliation across repeated runs
findings.body: AC15(d) says repeated runs yield one confirmed-defect universe, but a finding may be published or categorized differently across runs. The spec does not define which run's pass record or adjudication fixes category membership for the defect. Add a reconciliation rule for repeated-run evidence.

findings.title: Define cohort cutoff event and visibility
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) close the eligible cohort by a 'recorded cutoff' before findings are visible and refer to passes that 'completed'. They do not define the cutoff event, timestamp source, or what makes findings visible. Specify these so cohort closure is testable.

findings.title: Define unexpected findings for precision fixtures
findings.body: Use Case 4 and AC9 count unexpected findings, but only clean precision fixtures are defined. If precision fixtures can have expected findings, the spec does not say what makes a finding unexpected. Define unexpected findings or restrict precision fixtures to clean expectations.

findings.title: Define whether failed or superseded sweep passes count as recorded sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: Evidence-tier promotion depends on the first recorded sweep-enabled real-pull-request review, and AC1 requires logs for failed or superseded sweep passes. The spec does not say whether a pass that ran the sweep but published no review counts as a recorded sweep-enabled review. Define the counting rule.

findings.title: Define per-category recall attribution for multi-category findings
findings.body: Findings may be recorded against multiple categories, and the spec requires per-category recall attribution in benchmark output. It does not define how a multi-category finding is attributed to categories for recall, risking double counting or ambiguous attribution. Add an attribution rule.

findings.title: Define handling of failed or aborted runs in evidence metrics
findings.body: AC8, AC11, and AC15(d) require every attempted run to enter evidence and compute recall, variance, and cost metrics, but they do not define how failed, aborted, or incomplete runs are represented in those metrics. Specify inclusion, exclusion, or failure values.

findings.title: Clarify precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says the effective value comes from the highest-precedence source and lists 'environment or workflow input' over the operator config file, but it does not order environment versus workflow input when both supply non-empty values. Define the precedence.

findings.title: Specify where the fixture-ready declaration is recorded
findings.body: AC17 and Use Case 5 require the operator's declaration that the extended fixture is ready as a gate basis to be recorded, but no Operational Visibility surface or evidence artifact is named. State where the declaration is recorded.

findings.title: Specify enablement key and allowed values or cite the existing source
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete key name and exact on/off values to planning. For testability, list the allowed values or directly cite the existing durability-mode switch vocabulary and key convention.

findings.title: Fix temporal wording in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says 'the pass record before review', but the per-category pass record is written during or after review execution and before adjudication. Correct the wording to reflect the intended sequence.

findings.title: Remove duplicated 'used.' in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains the sentence fragment '... the runs used. used. It reports...'. Remove the duplicate word.

findings.title: Remove stray fragment in decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The Claim admissibility row's example ends with a stray lower-case fragment: 'they do not pair the claim.' Remove or integrate the sentence.

findings.title: Clarify 'only two tests' gating wording
findings.body: The business rule says 'only two tests are gating' and then lists four evidence types plus no precision regression. Rephrase to avoid implying that only two evidence types are involved.

findings.title: Use consistent hyphenation for per-finding resolution
findings.body: The spec alternates between 'per-finding resolution' and 'per-finding-resolution'. Pick one spelling for consistency.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful contracts, including the Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix, but the Document Quality Gate log in the PR description has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row so the gate log matches the checklist.

findings.title: Define how matched sweep-off controls are recorded without publishing
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(d) require a sweep-off review of the same real-pull-request heads, recorded but not published, for comparative claims. AC2 and the business rules preserve one review per head SHA and say the sweep adds no second publication path, while only benchmark runs are explicitly allowed to publish nothing. The spec never defines the execution/publication contract for a real-PR sweep-off control, so implementers cannot satisfy both the control requirement and the one-review contract.

findings.title: Reconcile precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: Business Rules say precision evidence must be on the same category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity as the claim. AC15(d), the evidence-tier enum, and the claim-admissibility matrix additionally require AC9 precision evidence on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count as the real-PR comparison. AC9 is benchmark fixture evidence, so same target/fixture/sample cannot be met for real-PR heads. State the exact precision evidence required for real-PR recall claims.

findings.title: Define cutoff artifact and proof it was fixed in advance
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the business rules close the eligible cohort by a 'recorded cutoff fixed in advance, before any eligible pass's findings are visible', but do not define the cutoff form, where it is recorded, or what evidence proves it was fixed before findings were visible. Without that, the ten-pull-request gate cannot be audited deterministically.

findings.title: Define 'pass completed' for cohort eligibility
findings.body: Use Case 6 says eligible pull requests are those whose pass completed by the cutoff, while AC1 distinguishes reaching review execution, completing review execution, publication, and terminal failure. Specify which event makes a pull request eligible for the closed cohort.

findings.title: Make sweep-claim membership test deterministic
findings.body: AC15(d) says a published finding's membership is the 'objective match' and that a per-category record or adjudication entry only records the verdict, but it provides no rule for determining the objective match when records conflict or when adjudication later maps a finding to a category. The confirmed-defect denominator therefore cannot be tested or audited. Define the authoritative membership rule and how mismatches are resolved and recorded.

findings.title: Define counting for pull requests with multiple eligible heads
findings.body: AC15(b) counts ten pull requests, but Ronda reviews each head SHA and a pull request can have multiple sweep-enabled reviews or external reviews. The spec does not say whether multiple eligible heads on one pull request count once or multiple times, nor which head's adjudication or clean result governs the pull-request count.

findings.title: Resolve precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says the effective value is from the highest-precedence source and lists 'environment or workflow input over the operator config file', but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty conflicting values. This is required to resolve sweep enablement deterministically.

findings.title: Define handling of failed or incomplete matched runs
findings.body: AC15(d) and AC11 require paired per-head or per-run metrics over whole cohorts or run sequences, but do not state what happens when a matched sweep-off control run, sweep-on run, or cost capture fails or is incomplete. Since subsets are prohibited, specify whether the whole claim becomes inadmissible or how failed runs are recorded and treated.

findings.title: Clarify zero-denominator rule when findings are rejected or out of scope
findings.body: AC15(d) defines zero denominator as no confirmed defects and parenthetically requires external reviews confirmed clean. If external or Ronda findings exist but are terminal ronda_better or ronda_rejected, there may be no confirmed defects while reviews are not clean. State whether recall and variance are not applicable in that case and how the clean-result language applies.

findings.title: Specify terminal miss outcomes when a sweep-off control exists
findings.body: AC15(b) and the business rules say a human-recorded defect within the sweep's claim, when all compared reviewers reported no findings, is terminally adjudicated only when recorded as a confirmed miss for the sweep-enabled review and external reviewer. If a sweep-off control is also a compared reviewer, the spec does not say whether the control must also receive a terminal miss or outcome, leaving counted status ambiguous.

findings.title: Specify treatment of human-recorded defects outside the sweep claim
