findings.body: AC15(d) includes human-recorded defects only when within the sweep's claim, but AC15(b)'s clean-result and terminal-adjudication rules do not say whether a human-recorded defect outside the claim must receive an outcome or can coexist with a clean result. This affects whether a pull request is terminally adjudicated and counted.

findings.title: Define the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record
findings.body: Use Case 6, the business rules, and AC15(d) permit a 'descriptive sweep-enabled miss record' at Real-PR evidence (measured), but no section defines its required fields, storage surface, or how it differs from an effect claim. Without that, the permitted claim boundary cannot be tested.

findings.title: Define unexpected-finding counting for precision evidence
findings.body: Use Case 4 and AC9 require unexpected-finding counts and a strict regression test across multiple runs, but do not say whether identical unexpected findings in repeated runs are counted per run or deduplicated, nor how fixtures that do not expect a clean result define 'unexpected'. The regression result can vary depending on the interpretation.

findings.title: Define when recording a control reopens adjudication
findings.body: Evidence-tier transitions and AC15(c) demote measured evidence when a sweep-off control recorded on a head 'reopens' adjudication, but do not define whether a control with no findings reopens a clean adjudication, what terminal outcome is required, or when the count is restored.

findings.title: Avoid implementation details in AC1
findings.body: AC1 prescribes bounded retry, check-run recovery state, and non-zero process exit. These are implementation mechanisms. State the observable product or log outcomes instead, or move the mechanism details to planning or implementation notes.

findings.title: Correct mirror-surface references in decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix cites 'Business rule' at approximately lines 106 and 120 for enablement and list readability, but those passages are in Use Case 1 considerations; the corresponding business rules appear later. Update mirror references to the normative sections.

findings.title: Remove or qualify 'only site' claim for adjudication code values
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values → Adjudication outcomes says it is the only site that fixes the new code values, but AC15(d) restates `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected`. Either remove the restatement or qualify the 'only site' claim.

findings.title: Identify the documentation required by AC17
findings.body: AC17 says 'Documentation states' the benchmark is not a regression gate until AC12 and AC13 exist, but does not identify which document or artifact must carry the statement. Name the target documentation or evidence artifact.

findings.title: Specify record for terminal failures that reach zero categories
findings.body: AC1 says a terminal failure after review execution logs the categories reached; if failure occurs before any review request, reached categories are zero. The spec does not say whether an empty per-category record is emitted or how logs represent zero reached categories.

findings.title: Clarify per-category surface when public review exists after late failure
findings.body: AC1 says when a review is already public and a later write fails, the record is on the logs 'with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced'. If that write produced a check run whose outcome is a review, the general rule requires the record on check-run output as well. State both surfaces explicitly to avoid a logs-only reading.

findings.title: State recognized on/off vocabulary or reference it
findings.body: AC18 defers exact on/off values to the plan while making unrecognized non-empty values off. For testability, enumerate the accepted values or normatively cite the existing durability-mode switch vocabulary.

findings.title: Add missing Matrix coherence preflight row to the Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The PR description's Document Quality Gate log includes rows such as Brief coverage, Internal consistency, and Complex workflow decision-gate matrix, but it has no `Matrix coherence preflight` row. The spec contains stateful constructs, including `Statuses / Enum Values → Evidence tier` valid transitions and the `Decision-gate consistency matrix`. The checklist requires the quality-gate log to carry the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable for stateful contracts. Add the missing row.

findings.title: Make AC9/AC15(d) precision pairing for real-PR recall claims testable
findings.body: AC15(d) says a comparative real-pull-request recall claim requires the paired precision evidence AC9 defines `on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count`, while also requiring the same category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity as the real-PR heads. Real pull-request heads are not fixture targets and have no fixture version, and AC9 itself speaks of precision fixtures rather than real-PR heads. As written, the requirement cannot be satisfied or tested for real-PR recall claims. Clarify whether the precision evidence must be benchmark-fixture evidence paired by model/list/configuration only, or define what target and fixture version mean for a real-PR claim.

findings.title: Define terminal outcome/record for human-recorded defects with no compared finding
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the business rules define terminal adjudication in terms of every compared finding carrying a terminal outcome or a clean result. AC15(d) also counts defects that human adjudication records even when no compared reviewer reported them. For the all-clean case where human adjudication records a defect, the spec says the PR is terminally adjudicated only when that defect is recorded as a confirmed miss for the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer, but no outcome code, schema, or terminal record is defined. The adjudication enum only adds `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected`, which cover Ronda-reported findings. Define the terminal outcome or record for human-recorded defects.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory membership rule in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says that, for a finding the pass published, membership in the sweep's claim is determined `by its per-category pass record entry`, but then says no recorded entry decides membership and that a run entry recording a membership the test contradicts is a misrecording carrying no membership. It does not state an objective, testable membership test beyond matching against category descriptions and failure shapes. This leaves the confirmed-defect denominator ambiguous and untestable. Specify the authoritative membership test, what evidence records the verdict, and how conflicts between pass records and adjudication are resolved.

findings.title: Require adjudication records to carry swept-category membership
findings.body: AC15(d) makes membership depend on adjudications naming the swept category for external-reviewer findings and for defects only human adjudication records. No Statuses/Enum Values entry or acceptance criterion defines an adjudication category field, its allowed values, or how `uncategorized` is recorded for adjudicated findings. Without that contract, the required membership decisions cannot be recorded or verified. Add an explicit adjudication-membership field or enum requirement.

findings.title: Specify enablement key and allowed on/off values in AC18
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete key name to planning and says the plan states the exact on/off values, while only referring to the existing durability-mode vocabulary. The sweep enablement gate is a behavioral contract, and its allowed configuration values should be explicit in the spec or incorporated by reference with the actual values enumerated. State the key name and allowed values, or make the external source normative and identifiable.

findings.title: Define precedence between environment and workflow input in AC18
findings.body: AC18 says the effective value is resolved through existing precedence as `environment or workflow input over the operator config file over the built-in default`, but it does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply different non-empty values. Because the decision gate depends on the effective value, this conflict rule must be explicit.

findings.title: Clarify cohort closure cutoff relative to visible findings
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) close the eligible cohort as pull requests whose sweep-enabled passes completed by a recorded cutoff fixed in advance, before any eligible pass's findings are visible. A completed pass normally publishes its review and makes findings visible, so the timing is ambiguous or potentially impossible. Define the cutoff event or timestamp precisely and explain how it prevents post-hoc cohort selection.

findings.title: Provide initial list version, activation date, and revision history
findings.body: The initial category list in `Statuses / Enum Values` does not define a list version, the date the version became current, or a revision-history entry. AC7 requires a version, revision history, activation date, and never-reused versions; AC19 treats missing or unidentifiable list versions as malformed. The spec should either provide the initial version/date/revision record or state exactly where that recorded artifact lives.

findings.title: Define treatment of failed/incomplete runs in measurement criteria
findings.body: AC8, AC11, and AC15(d) define per-run recall, variance, and cost evidence but do not state how terminal failures, unpublished runs, or missing heads within a run affect those metrics. AC1 defines per-category `not determined` for failed passes, but the measurement contract does not say whether such runs are included, excluded, counted as zero recall, or make evidence inadmissible. Define the handling so recall/variance/cost evidence is testable.

findings.title: Clarify AC11 cost metric pass/run relationship
findings.body: AC11 requires `model calls per pass` and `elapsed time per pass`, then defines a comparative benchmark cost metric as a per-run difference paired by run position. It does not define how a benchmark run maps to passes when a run reviews multiple heads or when a pass has multiple model-call phases. This leaves the cost aggregation ambiguous. Define which pass or passes are measured and how run-level cost figures are derived.

findings.title: State assumption/availability for historical model in AC8
findings.body: AC8 requires baseline comparability for the original-thirteen subset using the original fixture version with the historical model and configuration held constant. If the historical model version is no longer available, the requirement may be impossible to satisfy. State the assumption that the historical model remains available, or define an allowed substitute/fallback so the criterion remains testable.

findings.title: Align AC13 harder-credential wording with exhaustive ways
findings.body: AC13 says a harder case plants a sensitive `name or value` not matched by the canonical form, but the exhaustive four ways only cover name/wrapping variants and do not include value-only variants. Either add value-only variation to the exhaustive list or remove `value` from the general description to avoid ambiguity.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off control in terminal miss for human-recorded defects
findings.body: In Use Case 6, AC15(b), and the business rules, when all compared reviewers report no findings but human adjudication records a defect within the sweep's claim, terminal adjudication requires recording the defect as a confirmed miss for the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer. If a sweep-off control is recorded, it is also a compared reviewer/configuration and should receive a miss/outcome for that defect. Extend the terminal-miss rule to cover all recorded compared configurations.

findings.title: Name excluded never-found kinds in the excluded candidates list
findings.body: `Statuses / Enum Values` excludes `The seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds` as a group, while AC6 requires candidates to be named as excluded with rationale. The four kinds are named only in Use Case 2 considerations. List the four never-found kinds explicitly in the excluded-candidates record.

findings.title: Clarify ronda_rejected label when external reviewer also raised finding
findings.body: The adjudication outcomes section says `ronda_rejected` applies when Ronda's own review raised a finding, including when both Ronda and the external reviewer raised it. The display label `Ronda finding rejected` can then mislabel an external finding that is also being closed. Clarify the label/description or state explicitly that the outcome may close both Ronda and external compared findings for the same defect.

findings.title: Remove restated outcome code values from AC15(d) or relax the only-site rule
findings.body: `Statuses / Enum Values → Adjudication outcomes` says it is the only site that fixes the new code values and that other sites enumerate outcomes by concept. AC15(d), however, explicitly restates the code values `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected`. Either remove the code values from AC15(d) or revise the only-site statement.

findings.title: Define sweep pass or scope AC3/AC20 to passes that actually ran the sweep
findings.body: AC20 says every finding published by a `sweep pass` appears in the per-category pass record, and AC3 ties the review-summary statement to a `sweep pass`. AC18/AC19 also describe enabled passes that degrade to ordinary non-sweep reviews and emit no per-category record. The spec defines `sweep-enabled review` but not `sweep pass`. If a degraded enabled pass is a sweep pass, AC20/AC3 conflict with AC18/AC19; if not, say so. Define the term or scope those criteria to passes that actually ran the sweep.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs, including Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix. The PR's Document Quality Gate log has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row; the existing 'Complex workflow decision-gate matrix' bullet is not the required preflight audit.

findings.title: Define the sweep-off control run contract
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(d) require a matched sweep-off control that is recorded but not published, but no business rule, use case, or acceptance criterion defines how such a control pass is initiated, kept unpublished, identified, or what surfaces record its findings and cost. This leaves the control required by AC15(d) untestable and potentially conflicts with AC2's normal publication path. Define a control-run mode or evidence-record contract.

findings.title: Fix impossible precision pairing for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Claim admissibility matrix require paired precision evidence from AC9 'on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count' for a comparative real-PR recall claim, while also tying it to the real-PR heads' model identity, category-list version, and effective sweep configuration. Real-PR comparisons have no fixture target, fixture version, or benchmark sample count, and the Evidence tier real_pr_measured row states a narrower pairing. Clarify whether benchmark precision evidence is required and, if so, exactly which target, fixture, and sample count it must match; as written the requirement cannot be tested.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory membership rule in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for a pass's own finding is determined by its per-category pass record, then says membership is an objective match and that no recorded entry decides membership, with a conflicting record treated as a misrecording carrying no membership. This leaves no authoritative, testable source for membership. State which record or adjudication decides membership and how misrecordings are corrected.

findings.title: Require adjudications to record swept-category membership
findings.body: AC15(d) makes membership for external findings and human-only defects depend on the adjudication naming a swept category, but no acceptance criterion or business rule requires adjudication records to include a swept category or defines the outcome when no category is named. Add a recording requirement and a default out-of-claim rule.

findings.title: Clarify duplicate versus Ronda-only outcomes with multiple Ronda configurations
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Adjudication outcomes table do not say how to classify a defect found by both sweep-on and sweep-off configurations but not by the external reviewer. 'duplicate' is described as both reviewers found it, while 'ronda_only' covers a valid defect the external reviewer did not find. Define the outcome and numerator treatment for this multi-Ronda-configuration case.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off control in terminal miss rule
findings.body: Use Case 6, AC15(b), and the evidence-tier text say a human-recorded defect that no reviewer reported is terminal only when recorded as a confirmed miss for the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer. If a sweep-off control is recorded and also missed the defect, the spec does not say whether its miss must also be terminal. Add the control to the terminal miss record or state why it is excluded.

findings.title: Use a shared denominator in the zero-denominator rule
findings.body: AC15(d) says 'a configuration whose denominator is zero' reports recall not applicable, but the confirmed-defect denominator is defined for the head set and is common to both configurations. Rephrase to avoid implying per-configuration denominators.

findings.title: Define 'sweep pass' versus enabled or degraded pass
findings.body: AC3, AC10, and AC20 use 'sweep pass', while AC19 allows an enabled pass to degrade to an ordinary non-sweep review. The spec does not define whether a degraded enabled pass is a sweep pass for summary and metadata rules. Define the term or replace it with 'pass that actually ran the sweep'.

findings.title: State or anchor the recognized on/off configuration values
findings.body: AC18 defers the exact on/off values to the plan while making unrecognized non-empty values a distinct recorded off path. For testability, list the recognized values or cite the existing durability-mode switch contract that defines them.

findings.title: Address unavailable historical model for original-fixture comparability
findings.body: AC8 requires repeated original-fixture runs with the historical model and configuration held constant. If the historical model is retired or unavailable, the spec provides no alternative or exception. State the assumption or define a fallback evidence rule.

findings.title: Define cohort-cutoff evidence
findings.body: AC15(b) requires the eligible cohort cutoff to be recorded and fixed in advance before findings are visible, but no rule says what metadata records the cutoff or how an auditor verifies it. Add a record requirement for the cutoff and cohort membership.

findings.title: Add an acceptance criterion for credential-free logs
findings.body: Operational Visibility says logs never record credential values, but no business rule or acceptance criterion enforces it; AC14 only covers quality evidence. Add a testable rule covering logs and other sweep records.

findings.title: Clarify terminal failure before any review request
findings.body: AC1 says a pass that reaches review execution but fails before issuing a review request has reached no categories. It is unclear whether such a pass must emit an empty per-category log record or no record beyond the existing failure. State the expected log content for this edge case.

findings.title: Clarify AC1 surface rule when review is already public
findings.body: AC1 says that when the review is already public the per-category record is on the logs 'with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced'. This can read as logs-only even when the write produced a review-outcome check run, which would contradict the earlier rule that the check-run output carries the record when such a check run exists. Restate that the check-run output is included when it exists.

findings.title: Replace approximate line-number references in decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix cites mirror surfaces with approximate line numbers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. Line numbers will drift as the document changes. Replace them with stable section headings or rule names.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful contracts, including Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix, but the PR description's Document Quality Gate log has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row to the gate log.

findings.title: Fix impossible precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Claim admissibility matrix require a comparative real-pull-request recall claim to be backed by AC9 precision evidence 'on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count' as the real-PR comparison. Real-pull-request comparisons have no fixture version and their target is real heads, not precision fixtures, so the requirement cannot be satisfied as written. Restate the pairing requirements for real-PR recall claims in terms of the real-PR evidence set, or explicitly define the benchmark precision evidence that must accompany it.

findings.title: Zero-denominator rule does not cover excluded external findings
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 define the zero-denominator case as requiring external reviews' clean results, but the confirmed-defect denominator can also be zero when external findings exist and all are excluded from the measurement, for example as `ronda_better`. Clarify that zero denominator means no confirmed defects after terminal adjudication, including cases where external findings were all rejected, noisy, irrelevant, or out of scope.

findings.title: Define how repeated real-PR runs are recorded under one-review-per-head
findings.body: AC15(d) requires repeated identical runs on the same real pull-request heads for variance claims, while the Business Rules and AC2 preserve one review per head SHA. The spec does not define whether these repeated runs are unpublished measurement runs, how their findings are recorded, how they become compared reviewers, or how the first published review interacts with later repeated runs. Specify the recording and publication contract for repeated real-PR measurement runs.

findings.title: Define whether terminally failed sweep passes count as sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: AC1 gives per-category records for passes that reach review execution and then fail terminally, but the Business Rules define a sweep-enabled review as one whose pass ran the sweep and reported a list version, and AC15(b) counts pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review. It is unclear whether a terminally failed pass with no published review counts toward evidence-tier promotion or the ten-pull-request gate, and how its compared findings are adjudicated when there is no published Ronda result. State the treatment explicitly.

findings.title: Operational Visibility log statement conflicts with degraded cases
findings.body: Operational Visibility says logs record that the sweep ran, the list version, and the per-category pass record without qualification, but AC18 and AC19 require unrecognized-enablement and sweep-did-not-run records and no list version for degraded passes. Qualify the log statement so it applies only to passes that actually ran the sweep, and separately state the degraded and unrecognized log records.

findings.title: Enumerate recognized on/off enablement values or cite exact vocabulary
findings.body: AC18 defers the exact on/off values to planning and only references the durability-mode switch vocabulary. For a testable operator-configuration contract, the spec should enumerate the recognized on and off values or incorporate the existing vocabulary by explicit reference rather than leaving implementers to infer them.

findings.title: Define membership recording for defects found in only some repeated runs
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership is decided by the per-category pass record for findings a pass published, but repeated runs may publish a finding in some runs and not others. The spec does not say how the cohort-level membership for that defect is recorded for runs without a pass entry, or which record governs when a later adjudication maps the defect to a swept category. Define the membership evidence for intermittent findings.

findings.title: Specify required category-membership field in adjudication records
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for external reviewer findings and human-recorded defects to name the swept category matched, but Statuses/Enum Values -> Adjudication outcomes only defines outcome code values and does not define a category or membership field. Add the required adjudication metadata to the enum, dependency contract, or an acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Clarify per-category surface when post-publication check-run write fails
findings.body: AC1's general rule says check-run output carries the per-category record only when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. For a success check-run write that fails after bounded retry after the review is public, AC1 says the record is on the logs 'with whatever per-category surface its own check-run write actually produced.' This leaves it unclear whether the check-run output may also carry the record when the landed check run is not a review outcome. Reconcile these statements.

findings.title: Avoid implementation-dependent failure-ordering assumptions in AC1
findings.body: AC1 and the pass-outcome matrix classify a rejected model credential as failing after changed files are read and refer to bounded retry, check-run recovery state, and non-zero process exit. These are implementation details that may not be stable or observable from the product contract. Define the per-category surface requirements in terms of observable pass outcomes, such as published review, failure check run, and logs, without assuming specific failure ordering or retry internals.

findings.title: State assumption about superseded passes and check runs
findings.body: AC1 asserts that a pass superseded before publication writes no check run and therefore logs only. If the existing supersede path can write a non-review check run, the surface assignment rule would need to handle it. Either state that existing superseded passes never write check runs or cover the non-review check-run case explicitly.

findings.title: List the four never-found seeded kinds individually in excluded candidates
findings.body: The excluded-candidates record groups the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds as a single bullet, while Use Case 2 names them. Since AC6 requires the recorded list to account for every candidate, enumerate the four kinds in the excluded-candidates record itself.

findings.title: Define handling of equal variance figures
findings.body: AC15(d) requires a variance claim to be compared as a direction, higher or lower, with both standard deviations recorded, but does not say what happens when the two population standard deviations are equal. State that equality supports no direction or claim, or is reported as no change.

findings.title: Specify elapsed-time units and measurement point
findings.body: AC11 and AC15(d) require elapsed time per pass but do not state the unit or the interval being measured, for example wall-clock from pass start to completion excluding queue time. Define the unit and measurement boundary so cost evidence is comparable.

findings.title: Avoid approximate line-number references in decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix uses mirror-surface references like (~106), (~120), and (~541). Line numbers are unstable in a spec and can become contradictory after edits. Replace them with stable section or acceptance-criterion references.

findings.title: Clarify precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says environment or workflow input over the operator config file but does not state which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. If existing precedence already defines this, reference it explicitly; otherwise state the rule.

findings.title: Define fallback when historical model is unavailable for original-fixture comparability
findings.body: AC8 requires original-fixture baseline comparability with the historical model and configuration held constant. If the historical model is retired or unavailable, the spec provides no alternative, waiver path, or required documentation. State whether the comparison is impossible, what the evidence record must say, or what substitute evidence is admissible.

findings.title: Define how cohort cutoffs are recorded and repeated
findings.body: AC15(b) requires the eligible cohort to be closed before adjudication using a recorded cutoff, but does not define what form the cutoff takes, where it is recorded, or how a new cohort is opened if the first closed cohort has fewer than ten counted pull requests. Specify the cutoff record contract.

findings.title: Define cost handling for failed or missing per-head passes
findings.body: AC15(d)'s paired per-head cost metric assumes both configurations have model-call and elapsed-time figures for every head in the closed cohort. It does not say what happens if a pass failed, was skipped, or has missing cost data. State whether such heads are excluded, how that affects whole-cohort coverage, or whether the cost claim is inadmissible.

findings.title: Clarify defect-weighted recall terminology
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 3 use 'defect-weighted recall' but define it as confirmed defects reported over confirmed defects on the whole head set, which is an unweighted aggregate recall. Use one term or define the weighting explicitly.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs, including the Evidence tier transition table and the Decision-gate consistency matrix. The PR description's Document Quality Gate log has no 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row because the stateful contract exists.

findings.title: Resolve conflict over list-version logging for passes that publish no review
findings.body: Use Case 1 postconditions say a pass that publishes no review 'owes no activation statement or list version, whichever surface it otherwise writes'. Operational Visibility says logs record the list version for sweep passes, and Business Rules define a 'sweep-enabled review' as one whose pass reported a category list version as used. This leaves terminal-failure and superseded passes untestable and affects the ten-pull-request count. Clarify whether unpublished sweep passes record a list version, on which surfaces, and whether they can count as sweep-enabled reviews.

findings.title: Define terminal adjudication for human-recorded defects with no reviewer findings
findings.body: AC15(d) includes defects recorded only by human adjudication in the confirmed-defect denominator, but AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the evidence-tier rules allow a pull request whose compared reviewers reported no findings to be counted as clean once the external review confirms clean. No terminal outcome is defined for a human-only recorded defect in that situation, so a pull request can be counted as clean while a confirmed defect exists. Add an outcome or terminal rule for human-only defects and prevent clean counting when they exist.

findings.title: Specify how matched sweep-off controls on real pull request heads are recorded without publishing
findings.body: AC15(d), Use Case 6, and the business rules require a matched sweep-off control on the same real pull request heads, described as recorded but not published. The spec only defines benchmark runs as non-publishing and otherwise applies the one-review-per-head contract to passes that publish to GitHub. It does not define a control-run mode, its evidence surfaces, or how it avoids conflicting with the publication contract. Define the recording path and surfaces for real-PR sweep-off controls, or remove the requirement.

findings.title: Clarify precision-evidence pairing for benchmark and real-PR recall claims
findings.body: Business Rules, AC9, and AC15(d) require precision evidence on the 'same target, model, fixture version, and sample count' as the recall comparison. Precision fixtures are separate clean fixtures, and real-pull-request recall claims do not have a fixture version in the same sense. As written, claim admissibility is ambiguous and potentially untestable. State precisely which target and fixture version precision evidence must use for benchmark recall claims and for real-PR recall claims.

findings.title: Define model calls per pass and elapsed time per pass measurement boundaries
findings.body: AC11 and AC15(d) make cost claims depend on 'model calls per pass' and 'elapsed time per pass', but the spec does not say whether retries, queued time, setup/teardown, publication calls, or failed attempts are included. Without those boundaries, comparative cost claims cannot be tested consistently. Define the metrics or reference an existing metric definition.

findings.title: State whether descriptive sweep-enabled miss records are allowed at provisional tier
findings.body: AC15(a) bars only 'effect claims' below Real-PR evidence (measured), and Use Case 6 says real-PR evidence is read as a descriptive record. However, the Decision-gate consistency matrix says descriptive real-pull-request claims are permitted at measured tier alone, while provisional evidence is only indicative. Resolve whether provisional evidence may publish a descriptive sweep-enabled miss record or only tier/count metadata.

findings.title: Define handling of eligible pull requests with no external review
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 say a pull request with no recorded external review is not adjudicated, while the closed eligible cohort must be fully terminally adjudicated before ten pull requests are counted. If any eligible pull request never receives a recorded external review, the count can be blocked indefinitely. Specify whether such pull requests can be excluded, how cutoffs avoid them, or what recovery path exists.

findings.title: Define 'effective sweep configuration'
findings.body: AC9, AC15(d), and the Coverage Matrix require evidence to share the 'effective sweep configuration', but the term is not defined. It could mean the enablement value, category-list version, degraded state, or the resolved operator-configuration result. Define the term or replace it with named fields such as enablement value, list version, and degradation reason.

findings.title: Remove code values from AC15(d) or adjust the only-site statement
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says it is the only site that fixes the code values and that no other site restates them, but AC15(d) explicitly names `ronda_only` and `ronda_rejected`. Either remove the code values from AC15(d) or soften the uniqueness statement.

findings.title: Address unavailable historical model for original-fixture comparability
findings.body: AC8 and Use Case 3 require repeated original-fixture runs with the historical model and configuration held constant. If the historical model is deprecated or unavailable, the requirement cannot be met. State a fallback, equivalence rule, or record this as an explicit assumption/deferred decision.

findings.title: Clarify check-run record for terminal failures after public review
findings.body: AC1 says that for failures after the review is public the per-category record is on the logs 'in either case', but the general rule and the decision-gate matrix say the check-run output also carries the record when the pass's own write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. Make AC1 explicitly state logs plus check-run output when the success check run landed.

findings.title: Specify what a recorded cutoff contains
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 close the eligible cohort by a 'recorded cutoff', but do not define the cutoff identity or where it is recorded. Define the minimum cutoff fields, such as date/time, SHA, pull-request range, or list version, so cohort closure is auditable.

findings.title: Define which external review confirms a clean result when multiple exist
findings.body: Several rules refer to 'the recorded same-head external review' in the singular. If multiple external reviews are recorded for a head, the spec does not say which one confirms a clean result or supplies compared findings. Specify a selection rule, such as latest recorded, all must agree, or a named corpus review.

findings.title: State precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says 'environment or workflow input over the operator config file' but does not state which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply different non-empty values. If existing precedence defines it, reference that rule explicitly; otherwise specify the order.

findings.title: Limit implementation-specific details in AC1
findings.body: AC1 describes bounded retry, check-run recovery state, and non-zero process exit. These are implementation mechanics. The product contract can be stated in observable outcomes; move these details to planning/implementation guidance or rephrase them as observable behavior.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs (Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix), but the PR's Document Quality Gate log has no `Matrix coherence preflight` row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the required row or rationale.

findings.title: Define adjudication for human-recorded defects before counting clean pull requests
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the real-pull-request business rule count a pull request as clean when every compared reviewer reported no findings and the external review is clean. AC15(d), however, includes defects recorded only by human adjudication in the confirmed-defect denominator. The spec never says whether such a human-recorded defect invalidates the clean result, what terminal outcome or code value it carries, or how the pull request becomes terminally adjudicated. This lets a pull request be counted as clean while contributing a confirmed defect. State that human-recorded defects are compared findings (or otherwise require terminal adjudication), define their outcome, and block clean-result confirmation when one exists.

findings.title: Make precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims testable
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Claim admissibility matrix require a comparative real-PR recall claim to carry paired precision evidence AC9 defines 'on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count' and also 'on the same category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and model identity as those heads'. AC9 precision evidence is fixture-based, while real-PR heads have no fixture version and are not the same target as a precision fixture. As written the requirement cannot be satisfied. Clarify which precision evidence pairs with real-PR recall claims and remove or qualify fixture-target attributes that do not apply.

findings.title: Specify recognized on/off configuration values or reference them unambiguously
findings.body: AC18 makes behavior depend on 'recognized on and off values' and on detecting unrecognized non-empty values, but defers the exact values to the plan and only says they are the same vocabulary as an existing switch. Without enumerating the allowed values or naming the authoritative existing definition, AC18's on/off/unrecognized cases cannot be tested from this spec. Add the value set or a normative reference.

findings.title: Require adjudication records to capture swept-category membership
findings.body: AC15(d) makes claim membership depend on adjudications 'naming the swept category' for external findings, sweep-off control findings, and human-only defects, and says membership decisions must be recorded before the claim is read. No acceptance criterion or enum requires adjudication records to include that category, defines its allowed values, or says what happens when it is missing. Add an explicit data requirement and failure mode so the membership rule is testable.

findings.title: Scope AC10 clean-result rule to sweep passes
findings.body: AC10 says 'A review pass that finds nothing for every swept category...' and 'This applies to a pass that reaches publication', without limiting it to a sweep pass. Because the spec says non-sweep behavior is unchanged, this could be read to impose a clean-result publication contract on non-sweep passes. Scope AC10 to a sweep-enabled pass that actually ran the sweep.

findings.title: Assign unrecognized-enablement record surfaces in AC1
findings.body: AC18 says the unrecognized-enablement record is written 'on the surfaces AC1 assigns', and Operational Visibility describes it, but AC1 itself only assigns per-category records and does not mention the unrecognized-enablement record. Add a cross-reference or explicit surface rule in AC1 to avoid relying on inference.

findings.title: Reconcile sweep-off category attribution between precision and real-PR evidence
findings.body: Use Case 4 says sweep-off findings are 'never attributed to a category' and the operator is not required to derive one. AC15(d) nevertheless requires category membership for sweep-off control findings through adjudication when computing real-PR confirmed defects. Clarify that the no-attribution rule applies only to precision-fixture evidence, or define how sweep-off control findings are categorized for real-PR claims.

findings.title: Define equal-variance outcome
findings.body: AC15(d) says a variance claim is compared as a direction (higher or lower) with both standard deviations recorded, but does not say what to report when the standard deviations are equal. State that equality is reported as no direction/no variance change, or define the allowed claim.

findings.title: State the check-run assumption for superseded passes
findings.body: AC1 and the pass-outcome matrix assign logs-only records for 'a pass superseded before publication' on the assumption that it 'writes no check run'. The spec does not define whether the existing flow may write a skipped, cancelled, or neutral check run in that case. If such a check run can exist, the surface rule is ambiguous. Explicitly state the existing-flow behavior or make the rule conditional on the check-run outcome.

findings.title: Define 'check run whose outcome is a review'
findings.body: AC1 and the Decision-gate consistency matrix repeatedly use 'a check run whose outcome is a review' as the trigger for check-run surface assignment, but the spec does not define that phrase or reference the existing definition. Add a definition or normative reference to avoid implementation guesswork.

findings.title: Address unavailable historical model for original-fixture comparability
findings.body: AC8 and Use Case 3 require repeated original-fixture runs 'with the historical model and configuration held constant' to restore baseline comparability. If the historical model is no longer available, this evidence requirement becomes impossible. State the assumption that the historical model remains available or define the fallback/exception for model unavailability.

findings.title: Clarify precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 states precedence as 'environment or workflow input over the operator config file over the built-in default', but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. If existing precedence defines this, reference it; otherwise specify the ordering.

findings.title: Identify the documentation artifact required by AC17
findings.body: AC17 says 'Documentation states' the benchmark gate status and deferred pass/fail contract, but does not identify which documentation artifact must carry the statement. Name the artifact or make AC17 checkable against the spec/evidence record.

findings.title: Clarify when a newly recorded control reopens a counted pull request
findings.body: AC15(c) and the evidence-tier transitions say a sweep-off control recorded on a head inside the cohort can demote the tier because its findings become compared findings. They do not say whether a control with no findings reopens the pull request or leaves the clean count unchanged. Clarify that only recorded control findings reopen adjudication.

findings.title: Define cohort status when a later control reopens adjudication
findings.body: AC15(b) requires the eligible cohort to be closed before adjudication, but AC15(c) and the evidence-tier transitions allow a sweep-off control recorded later to reopen a head's adjudication and change the count. The spec does not say whether the cohort cutoff changes, whether the cohort remains closed, or how claims made during the interim are treated. Define the cohort lifecycle for reopened adjudications.

findings.title: Define head selection for pull-request-level counts and claims
findings.body: AC15(b) counts pull requests, but Ronda's review contract and evidence are per head SHA. The spec does not say which head represents a pull request when multiple sweep-enabled reviews exist, whether later heads supersede earlier cohort membership, or which heads are included in matched controls, recall denominators, and cost pairs. Define a head-selection rule for cohort membership and comparative claims.

findings.title: Define 'pass completed' for cohort cutoff
findings.body: Use Case 6 step 1 defines the cohort as pull requests 'whose pass completed by a recorded cutoff', while AC15(b) says pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review. Because AC1 distinguishes review execution, publication, and check-run completion, 'completed' is ambiguous. State whether completion means published review, completed review execution, or another recorded outcome.

findings.title: Define how unpublished sweep-off controls are recorded
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require a matched sweep-off control on the same heads, 'recorded but not published'. The spec does not define the recording artifact, surface, or how a second same-head Ronda run avoids violating AC2's one-review-per-head contract. Define the control record mechanism and its relation to published reviews.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row to Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The plan contains a stateful contract: a decision-gate matrix, evidence-tier transitions, and operator-config precedence rules. The Document Quality Gate log therefore requires a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. The current log has only a complex workflow decision-gate matrix row, so the required audit is missing.

findings.title: Add plan authoring rigor outcome record
findings.body: The plan has no plan-authoring-rigor block or per-rule outcome record. The required block must name all six rules by canonical name, one line each in the required trigger form, name the three outcome labels, and link docs/workflow/development-workflow/plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md without restating pass conditions. A missing outcome record is blocking under the backstop rule.

findings.title: Correct implementation-order consistency claim and stale step references
findings.body: The Document Quality Gate claims implementation-order consistency is checked, but the plan and runbook contain conflicting implementation-step references. Examples: the recall-benchmark CLI flags are said to be specified in Implementation Order step 10 but are specified in step 11; Seed Data says the original-thirteen snapshot is taken before step 9 mutates the fixture, while step 10 mutates it; the smoke runbook says the snapshot is created in implementation step 9; and Implementation Order step 11 refers to the evidence doc as step 11 when it is step 12. Fix the references and the gate claim.

findings.title: Define degraded records for terminal failure and superseded passes
findings.body: The pass-orchestration steps emit the unrecognized-enablement and invalid-list degraded records on the success path, but AC18 and AC19 assign those records to the surfaces AC1 assigns. AC1 includes logs for terminal failure after the review request and for superseded completion without a review-outcome check run. The plan does not define or test degraded-record emission for those paths, leaving specified behavior unplanned.

findings.title: Provide per-finding category attribution for precision evidence
findings.body: AC9 requires each sweep-on unexpected precision finding to be attributed to its category, categories, or uncategorized. The planned classifyFindings result and SweepPassRecord only carry per-category outcomes and an uncategorized count, not a mapping from individual findings to categories. Without that mapping, the required precision evidence cannot be produced or tested as written.

findings.title: Specify how version-attestation basis is supplied and recorded
findings.body: The benchmark configuration block must carry an operator-recorded version-attestation basis, and AC8/AC9 admissibility depends on it, but the plan defines no flag, config key, file, or operator input source for that value. The implementer would have to invent the mechanism, so the step is not executable as written.

findings.title: Define benchmark behavior when sweep list is invalid
findings.body: The benchmark driver uses --sweep-mode on and drives list loading through the loader, but the plan does not say what happens when the list is unreadable, empty, or malformed during a benchmark run. AC19 degradation and AC1 benchmark surfaces imply a degraded record or an explicit reasoned exclusion, but neither is planned.

findings.title: Capture effective review configuration completely
findings.body: AC9 defines effective review configuration as every setting that can change what a review reports, including the review prompt, inference parameters, and immutable model version. The planned configuration block names maxPatchChars, a vague review configuration, prompt fingerprint, and reported model, but does not explicitly enumerate or record inference parameters. Make the captured fields explicit and complete.

findings.title: Reconcile matchTerms validation with AC19
findings.body: The validator treats a missing or empty matchTerms array as malformed, but AC19's malformed conditions do not include matchTerms. This adds a degradation trigger for a list that could satisfy the spec's required fields. Either justify this as a planning decision that remains consistent with the spec or remove the extra malformed condition.

findings.title: Enumerate matchTerms or define a deterministic selection rule
findings.body: The deterministic classifier and several tests depend on category matchTerms, but the plan only says they are non-empty lowercase substrings drawn from failureShape wording. Without exact values or a deterministic selection rule, classification behavior, seed matching, and AC9 attribution tests require implementation-time guessing.

findings.title: Make seed data concrete
findings.body: The new seed entries use paths such as src/benchmark/git-history.ts or similar and describe scenarios without exact patch content, expected representative findings, or concrete classifier fixtures. AC12, AC13, and the seed-matching tests need enough specificity to implement and verify without guessing.

findings.title: State whether campaign JSON output files are committed artifacts
findings.body: Implementation Order writes benchmark campaign outputs to docs/testing/ronda/sweep-*.json, and the evidence document is assembled from those files, but the plan does not say whether those JSON files are committed, retained, or cleaned up. Generated artifacts should be called out explicitly so evidence remains inspectable.

findings.title: Assert sub-themes below candidate boundary in scenario 8
findings.body: AC6 requires the recorded list to name the sub-themes below the candidate boundary. Testing Strategy scenario 8 asserts swept and excluded candidates but does not assert that the below-boundary sub-themes are present. Add that assertion so AC6 verification is complete.

findings.title: Extend credential scan to committed evidence artifacts
findings.body: Scenario 7's credential scan walks seeds and fixture files under the benchmark tree, but AC14 applies to quality evidence produced by the feature, including committed evidence documents under docs/testing/ronda. Either include those evidence files in the scan or provide a reasoned alternative.

findings.title: Fix AC1 assertion checklist terminal-failure statement
findings.body: The Assertions Checklist says terminal failures after the request record not_determined on the logs only. That contradicts Step 6 and AC1, which require ordinary produced_findings or produced_none values when the failure occurs after the review is already public. Update the checklist to include the post-publication exception.

findings.title: Replace conditional documentation update wording
findings.body: Documentation updates such as index the new runbook if that file's conventions require it and add sweep mode only if those docs enumerate every review mode are vague. State the exact condition, verification step, or intentional omission to avoid implementation-time guessing.

findings.title: Align decision-gate count with spec
findings.body: The Document Quality Gate says the item adds five decision gates and one pass-outcome rule, while the spec describes four decision gates and one pass-outcome rule. Clarify the classification so the gate log and spec agree.

findings.title: Add the required Plan Authoring Rigor outcome record
findings.body: The plan contains no Plan Authoring Rigor block. REVIEW.md requires this block to name all six rules by their canonical names, one line each, name the three outcome labels, link plan-authoring-rigor-rules.md as the canonical statement, and record per-rule outcomes or Not applicable rationales. A missing outcome record is blocking per Group H. Add the required block to the plan.

findings.title: Add a Matrix coherence preflight row to the Document Quality Gate
findings.body: The plan has a stateful contract: its Decision-gate matrix, enablement precedence rules, pass-outcome surface rules, and evidence-tier transitions.
